statute: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge (2024)
title: Mandatory Patent Disclosure of Genetic Resources and Traditional Knowledge
content:
Adopted by consensus at WIPO in Geneva on May 24, 2024, the GRATK Treaty establishes a new international standard for patent transparency:
1. Status & Entry into Force (Article 17): The Treaty was adopted in 2024 and will enter into force three months after 15 eligible Contracting Parties deposit their instruments of ratification or accession. The mandatory disclosure obligations apply to patent applications filed in Contracting Parties once the Treaty enters into force for that party.
2. Mandatory Disclosure Obligation (Article 3): Where a claimed invention in a patent application is based on genetic resources, applicants must disclose the country of origin (or source if origin is unknown). Where based on associated traditional knowledge, applicants must disclose the indigenous peoples or local community who provided it (or source). If unknown, the applicant must submit a formal declaration.
3. Sanctions and Remedies (Article 6): Contracting parties must provide an opportunity to rectify failures to disclose before imposing sanctions. Crucially, Article 6.4 establishes that no Contracting Party shall revoke, invalidate, or render unenforceable a patent solely for failure to disclose, UNLESS there has been fraudulent intention or fraudulent misrepresentation as determined under national law.
4. Global Impact for Ayurveda: Provides an international framework to prevent erroneous patents on Indian traditional knowledge in foreign jurisdictions, complementing India's domestic disclosure regime under Section 10(4)(d) of the Patents Act.
